about.title: Rancho Cucamonga Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Six people died in Rancho Cucamonga traffic collisions in 2025, according to public crash records for San Bernardino County. Each of those numbers was a person, and behind each one is a family now sorting through grief while also facing questions about bills, income, and what happens next. Some of those losses happen on the freeways that frame the city, SR-210 and I-15, or along Foothill Boulevard, which carries some of the highest recorded collision counts in town. Others come from a fall at a property, a workplace incident, or a medical error. When a death traces back to someone else's negligence, California law gives certain family members the right to bring a wrongful death claim. That civil action is separate from any criminal case and can cover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Rancho Cucamonga families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: What a Wrongful Death Attorney Can Help You Sort Out

items.title: Who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where you fit and make sure the right people are part of the claim.

items.title: A two-year clock that can shrink
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the window is much shorter when a government entity is involved. Knowing which timeline applies early protects the claim.

items.title: Losses that go beyond the bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help document each of these so nothing is left out.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-210 or I-15 in Rancho Cucamonga. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. Freeway crashes sometimes raise questions about roadway design, signage, or maintenance, and if a public agency is a potential defendant, the deadline to act is far shorter than the usual two years. An attorney can look at the collision report and tell you quickly whether a government claim needs to be filed first.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution in San Bernardino County. The criminal case can sometimes provide useful evidence, but your two-year deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in court.

items.question: We cannot afford a lawyer right now. What does LawProactive cost?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle wrongful death claims on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery, so you can get answers without taking on another expense during an already hard time.
